---
title: "About"
---

## The name

An *emaki* (絵巻) is a Japanese picture handscroll: a long painted scene held
between two rolls of paper, read by winding it from one to the other, a span at
a time. It is a good name for a window whose job is a conversation too long to
see at once.

The app's icon is a handscroll seen from the front, with a conversation on its
sheet --- the agent on the left with its spark, your reply on the right. The
drawing on the home page is the same scroll, with a landscape on it, and it
winds as you move across it.

## Why it exists

Claude Code deletes its transcripts after `cleanupPeriodDays`, thirty by
default, with no warning. Every other tool in this space reads
`~/.claude/projects` and stops there, so they all inherit that expiry.

So Emaki copies first and renders second. The archive sweep runs before
anything else touches a session, for exactly this reason: if rendering fails,
the bytes are already safe. The archive is not a backup but a peer source ---
live and archived transcripts are unioned, so a session Claude Code has deleted
stays listed, searchable, renderable and exportable, flagged as *kept*.

Compaction, for what it is worth, was never the threat: it appends a boundary
and keeps writing to the same file, leaving the earlier rows intact.

## How it is built

Rust, with [GPUI](https://www.gpui.rs) --- the Zed editor's UI framework ---
and [gpui-component](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-component) for the
window. There is no daemon, no browser and no hook.

```
crates/emaki-core    everything without a window, plus the emaki-core CLI
crates/emaki-app     the window
vendor/              the gpui-component crates, with a few changes of ours
scripts/             packaging, the icon, the status line
```

The core works in this order:

1. **Adapters**, one per agent, find each agent's sessions on disk.
2. **Archive** copies them byte for byte, before anything else touches them.
3. **Build** parses the JSONL transcript into a model of rounds, items and tool
   calls. The transcript is the only source of truth.
4. **Render** writes that model as markdown under `~/.emaki/logs`.
5. **Search** indexes every item in SQLite FTS5.

The app reads the same model and draws it. A file watcher says when to look
again. To reply, it either writes to a terminal session's inbox socket or runs
a headless `claude -p --resume` child that appends to the same transcript.

## Where it is going

Three stages. The first is a complete app for Claude Code --- permanent
history, organization by recency, project and agent, readable conversations,
and an explanation on any step. The second is the public release and the
feedback that comes with it. The third extends the same features to Codex,
Kimi and the other mainstream coding agents, so Emaki works across all of
them.

Codex support landed in v0.2.0; the [releases](releases.qmd) are the honest
record of where things actually are.

## Credits

The home page's figure follows the line-drawing manner of
[hairline](https://github.com/lucasmarkes/hairline)'s figures: nothing filled,
no words, what is far is dimmer, and one bright mark.

Icons are [Tabler](https://tabler.io/icons)'s outline set, drawn at a stroke of
1.75 where Tabler's own is 2. The file tree's icons are
[Catppuccin](https://github.com/catppuccin/vscode-icons)'s. The code colours
are [Rosé Pine](https://rosepinetheme.com)'s hues, retinted for contrast. The
terminal keeps [Kaku](https://github.com/kakuapp)'s cream in the light
appearance. Every face the app carries is under the SIL Open Font License.
